title: Upper limb · photographed 20-item paper A
note: Three source photographs in printed question order (1–20), posted January 2025. Sitting date unconfirmed. Q10 has mismatched answer choices and is retained ungraded.

questions.prompt: Which joint classification is correct?
questions.note: Radioulnar joints are pivot synovial joints.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Infraglenoid tubercle gives origin to:
questions.note: Long triceps originates below the glenoid.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Trapezius attaches to all EXCEPT:
questions.note: Trapezius inserts on lateral clavicle, acromion and scapular spine.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which does not attach to the intertubercular groove region?
questions.note: Pectoralis minor attaches to coracoid.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which neurovascular statement is correct?
options: Anterior circumflex humeral artery and axillary nerve use triangular space
Radial nerve accompanies superior ulnar collateral artery
Musculocutaneous and radial nerves supply elbow flexors
Basilic vein is lateral to cephalic
questions.note: Biceps/brachialis are musculocutaneous supplied; brachioradialis is radial supplied.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which nerve group contributes to shoulder abduction?
questions.note: Supraspinatus, deltoid and trapezius contribute. Long thoracic/serratus also contributes above horizontal but is not listed.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which plexus statement is false?
questions.note: Suprascapular normally branches from upper trunk (C5–6), not directly from C5 ramus.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which innervation is incorrect?
questions.note: Teres major is lower-subscapular supplied.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: At its proximal arm course, median nerve lies relative to brachial artery:
questions.note: It starts lateral before crossing anteriorly to medial.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All are branches of radial artery EXCEPT:
options: Nerve to levator scapulae arises from C5
Ulnar nerve arises from medial cord
Thoracodorsal nerve arises from posterior cord
questions.note: The source prints nerve statements under an arterial stem. No choice answers it; retained without invented replacement options.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which tendon passes medial to Lister tubercle?
questions.note: EPL turns around the ulnar side of the dorsal radial tubercle.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which cubital-fossa statement is true?
options: Median nerve lies lateral to biceps
Radial nerve is deep to brachialis
Radial artery passes between pronator teres heads
Brachial artery lies deep to bicipital aponeurosis
questions.note: The aponeurosis protects the artery and median nerve from superficial venepuncture.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which does not form anterior axillary wall?
questions.note: Teres major contributes posteriorly.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Nerves responsible for wrist adduction are:
questions.note: FCU is ulnar and ECU radial supplied.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which snuffbox statement is true?
questions.note: Scaphoid and trapezium form the floor; EPL is medial and APL/EPB lateral.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which does not take the common extensor origin?
questions.note: EI is a deep extensor arising from ulna/interosseous membrane.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which passes through a compartment in the flexor retinaculum?
questions.note: FCR has a separate retinacular canal, outside the carpal tunnel proper.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which lumbrical statement is true?
options: They insert directly on proximal phalanges
They are supplied by ulnar and radial nerves
questions.note: Lumbricals arise from FDP and insert on extensor expansions; median/ulnar supply.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which superficial-palmar-arch statement is true?
options: It lies at level of distal border of outstretched thumb
It lies deep to FDS tendons
questions.note: This is the conventional surface landmark. The arch is mainly ulnar and superficial to long flexor tendons; contributions vary.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Carpal tunnel median-nerve injury causes all EXCEPT:
questions.note: Adductor pollicis is ulnar supplied; flexion is not totally lost because long flexor supply arises proximally.
questions.subject: anatomy

audit.method: Source photograph transcription; anatomy review; original defects preserved, multiple defensible choices accepted.
